status: current-policy evaluator trained and held-out; value-guided search failed confirmation

training_data.split: whole-roster-disjoint train/calibration/test; held-out search teams were separately sampled and had no roster overlap with training rosters
training_data.perspective_safety: all source rows passed the player-view information-boundary validator

heldout_metrics.interpretation: predictive for the Round600h training mixture, not an ideal-play or Nash value; opening estimates are materially weaker

round611_search_confirmation.teams: 512 evaluation rosters per opponent, all disjoint from Round600h training rosters
round611_search_confirmation.search: one midgame decision, 2 sampled hidden worlds, 4 own candidates x 4 responses, 4 chance samples, equilibrium selection; policy-only control
round611_search_confirmation.fallbacks: 26/512 attempts per opponent safely fell back: 14 Illusion preview ambiguities and 12 publicly observed Transform states; no match failures
round611_search_confirmation.decision: no supported gain; do not deploy or scale this search configuration

round612_response_coverage.status: diagnostic complete; 64 clusters per opponent, 256 matches per opponent
round612_response_coverage.measure: fraction of sampled worlds where the actual opponent joint action appeared in the four-action response shortlist
round612_response_coverage.interpretation: shortlist misses the realized joint response in 46.8% of Max Damage worlds and 67.1% of Public Counterplay worlds; action-slot marginal coverage is higher but does not guarantee a represented joint counter

next: Do not keep scaling the matrix blindly. Improve response proposal quality: evaluate policy-supported and strategically threatening joint actions, plus selective best-response generation to the current mixed strategy. Measure held-out joint-response coverage and exact/measured per-decision cost first; only then run a sufficiently powered paired match screen.

round613_same_team_selector_ablation.design: 64 same seeded clusters per opponent, both seats, four response candidates; compared semantic vs slot_coverage selector
round613_same_team_selector_ablation.score_note: Each side-swapped arm had only 64 clusters; raw/search score deltas are exploratory and too noisy for a strength claim.
round613_same_team_selector_ablation.conclusion: Slot coverage increases marginal per-slot coverage but does not improve full joint-action coverage.

round614_eight_response_ablation.design: 64 same seeded clusters per opponent, both seats; 4 own candidates x 8 responses, 4 chance samples, 2 hidden worlds
round614_eight_response_ablation.score_note: The 64-cluster score differences are exploratory and do not establish a strength change.
round614_eight_response_ablation.conclusion: More response columns improve coverage, but exact joint coverage remains below 62% and throughput falls about 39–42% versus the four-response diagnostic. This cost is too high without demonstrated match gains.
